title: As a mother
hookLine: as a mother protects her only child, so cultivate boundless love for all beings (Sutta Nipata 1.8)

lines: WHAT IF IT HAD NO EDGES?
cards: A toddler wobbles toward the edge of a pool. Across the yard, a mother is already moving, before she's even decided to. Nothing else matters for that second: no meeting, no phone, no pride.

There is one child, and she would put herself between that child and any harm. A short Buddhist text takes that instant, a fierce, protective love, and asks something startling. What if that love had no edges?

teach.b: In the Metta Sutta, the discourse on loving-kindness, the Buddha says, in paraphrase: just as a mother would protect her only child with her own life, so one should cultivate a boundless heart toward all beings.

Before that image comes a wish: may all beings be happy and at ease. Then the sutta spells out who all means. Weak or strong, long or short, large or small, seen or unseen, near or far, born or yet to be born.

Nobody is left out by size or distance, or even by not being born yet. The sutta asks this love to spread above, below and all around, without obstruction, hatred or enmity. A mother's love is narrow: one child.
The sutta keeps its intensity and takes away the walls. That's the turn.
And it's for all times: standing, walking, sitting or lying down, as long as one is awake.
Loving-kindness here isn't a mood for a quiet room; it goes wherever the body goes. The commentaries tell that the Buddha taught it to monks who were frightened in a forest.
In Theravada communities the sutta is still chanted, at home and in monasteries.

how: Theravada Buddhists chant the Metta Sutta at home and in monasteries, and some Buddhists practice metta meditation, wishing well first to themselves or loved ones and then to all beings.

o: a mother's duty to her own family
a calm mind, free of every feeling

games.q: inside the Metta Sutta — tap the pairs.
p: protects her only child with her life
may all beings be happy and at ease

s: the sutta's love is only for people close to you
it reaches weak or strong, near or far, seen or unseen, born or yet to be born.
the sutta uses a mother's love as its pattern
as a mother would protect her only child, so cultivate a boundless heart.
loving-kindness here is meant only for meditation
the sutta says to keep it standing, walking, sitting or lying down.

games.q: the sutta has a mother's fierce love for one child. what does it do with it?
o: say it's too attached and set it aside.
keep its intensity and take away the walls.
games.why: it holds the mother's love up as the pattern, then asks for it toward all beings, boundless.

practice: Bring to mind someone you'd protect without thinking, a child, a parent, a friend, a pet, and let that warmth come clearly.
Keeping it, let the sutta's wish move outward, may all beings be happy and at ease: to people on your street, then people near and far you don't know, then every creature, seen and unseen.
If the warmth thins, return to the one you'd protect and start again.

wordCard.voice: Metta. Loving-kindness, cultivated the way a mother would protect her only child, then stretched boundless toward all beings. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali: loving-kindness, the name of the Metta Sutta.

carryVoice: Your line: boundless. A mother's fierce love, with the walls taken away. Until tomorrow, then.
